why: The regression net derives what it drives FROM THE MANIFEST. `format_arm` uses a collapsed caret because that is the only gesture set-bold was offered for, and the runner says so in its own comment. So an action that is UNDER-offered is invisible to every check at once: the manifest narrows, the harness narrows with it, and the two agree forever. Finding 078 is what that costs -- the operator selected text, pressed bold, and got a refusal, while 38 checks were green. This file is the expectation kept OUTSIDE the manifest, so the two can disagree.
howToUse: check_gesture_offers.py compares the shipped profile's action map against `expected`. A narrowing is a FAILURE here even when every other check is green, and a widening is a failure too -- an action offered for a gesture nobody characterised is the defect this project's contract exists to prevent, in the other direction.
changing: Never edit `expected` to make this pass. Either the manifest is wrong, or a measurement has been taken and BOTH move together, with the evidence named in `rationale`.

rationale.set-bold: both range bits characterised 2026-08-23, all four inline formats, findings/evidence/f078-inline-format-on-a-selection/. BOTH are granted because the engine's gate requires both for a range it has not classified -- classifying needs the html read that findings 037/038 identify as a wedge -- so granting one alone admits nothing at all. Measured three ways: single-only refused, cross-only refused, both accepted. A fully selected paragraph writes paragraph-level formatting, which native LibreOffice 26.8 does identically.
rationale.select-all: shipped dark: present in the manifest with an EMPTY gesture list, which is what withholding means here. Omitting it would ship it wide open, because the engine initialises every action to all-permitted and intersects from there.
rationale.delete-selection: range only by nature; a collapsed caret has nothing to delete.

andSemantics: A NAMED LIMIT OF THIS SCHEMA. For a non-collapsed selection the engine requires BOTH range bits, because at that gate the selection has not been classified and classifying it needs a read that can wedge the engine. So `range-single` and `range-cross` are not independently grantable for actions that go through that gate: any expectation naming one without the other describes a profile that offers nothing. Recorded here so the next builder does not re-derive it by minting three profiles, which is how it was found.
profileNote: Moved v7 -> v8 on 2026-08-24 with finding 076's link. ONLY THIS FIELD MOVED: `expected` is byte-identical, and that is the point of it living outside the manifest -- a link is exactly the moment a product quietly narrows, and the v8 recipe passes --inline-range-gestures all so it does not. Verified before the link by dry-packaging a v8 manifest from v7's bytes and diffing the gesture map: identical.
